title: The Apology Tour
tagline: The resolution is still alive. The evidence is less cooperative.
premise: Your New Year's resolution has already gone slightly wrong, and the host gives a flat press statement about it. On each turn, add one new fact that makes the public explanation harder to believe while keeping the speaker talking. The Judge checks that each fact follows from the latest statement and makes the collapse worse.

seed_pool.opening_token: The official position is that I am finally taking work seriously.
The official position is that I am cutting back on unnecessary spending.
The official position is that I am becoming a calmer person.

tests: One New Year's resolution is stated as an official position, and a stranger can picture the setting at once. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can add one embarrassing fact within five seconds, and there is more than one good answer. Say two.
The card already has a small crack, not a full collapse. It invites evidence and explanation rather than ending the joke.
Nobody is harmed on the card, no real people, no brands, no protected groups, and no serious crime is required to understand it.
It sounds like a person making a weak public statement, not like a slogan, a diary entry, or a list of goals.

move_constraints.example: The official position is that I am saving money. The bank statement contains a charge for a life-size inflatable hot tub.
move_constraints.hint: Add one observable fact that makes the latest official position harder to believe.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much worse the public explanation becomes because of this fact.
rubric.anchors: 0 = the position is no worse, or the fact changes nothing; 1 = a small bruise to the story; 2 = the explanation now has a clear new problem; 3 = a new witness, place, or piece of evidence makes the position publicly awkward; 4 = the explanation reaches a much larger and still believable embarrassment in one step, rare. Reach is earned only when the fact connects. A huge unrelated scandal scores 0 here.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How directly the new fact grows out of the latest statement.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no connection is shown; 1 = the fact could belong to any story; 2 = the connection is possible but thin; 3 = a stranger immediately sees why this fact damages the statement; 4 = the fact feels like the exact evidence the statement was trying to hide, rare. A move that adds several explanations or facts at once scores no higher than 2 here.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the evidence.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no observable fact, or only a feeling or verdict; 1 = vague or abstract; 2 = clear but ordinary; 3 = a specific object, person, record, or action appears; 4 = one sharp detail makes the failed resolution instantly visible, rare. Extra words do not improve the picture by themselves.

criterion.description: A move FOLLOWS if it is one new, observable fact that directly makes the latest official position look worse and forces the next explanation. The fact should be stated plainly while the speaker keeps the official tone. A move fails when it skips links by inventing a distant scandal, adds several separate facts without showing the bridge, ends with a final confession, clears the speaker, or says the matter is closed, rewinds or retracts a fact already stated, replaces the situation with an unrelated one, or gives only a feeling or verdict instead of evidence.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, discussing the game, or explaining the rules instead of adding evidence is itself a broken move.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no latest statement from a player move: judge the fact against the opening card and ask whether it directly makes that official position harder to believe.

A new witness, place, or record may enter when the latest statement plainly gives them a reason to exist, such as a manager after a missed shift or a bank statement after a claim about saving money. A distant scandal with no shown bridge is a skipped link: satisfies_criterion is false.

An ending is any move that gives a final confession, clears the speaker, announces the truth is accepted, says the press conference is over, or otherwise leaves no explanation for the next player. Endings fail satisfies_criterion even when they follow from the latest fact.
A move that only repeats the same evidence or changes its wording without adding a new observable fact is a duplicate: not_semantic_duplicate is false.
A move that retracts, denies, deletes, or reverses a fact already stated is an undo: satisfies_criterion is false.
A move with two or three facts may pass only when each link is plain, but score link at 2 or below and picture low because the explanation is crowded.
A fact of the same small size still follows and passes the gate if it makes the position slightly worse. Do not fail it for being modest.
A feeling, intention, insult, or verdict is not evidence. The speaker being embarrassed is not the fact; the unopened gym bag beside the takeaway is.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
The joke carries the reason. A stranger who read only the latest statement and the new fact must see why the position got worse.
Name the resolution and the evidence, or their plain stand-ins. A headline that fits any failed plan is lazy.
Never open with a status word or a ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Press Secretary refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Mock the official statement and the evidence, and use roast-level jabs at the player when the move earns it. Never target identity, protected traits, disability, or real-world vulnerability.
Plain spoken English. Profanity and adult innuendo are allowed when they sharpen the joke. Do not make them the whole joke.
On a skipped link, name the missing bridge. On an ending, say the explanation closed and the chain stops here.
On a refusal, the headline refuses the move and asks for another. It never declares who won.
The coaching line names one observable fact that would have followed. It ends on evidence, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: Taking work seriously now includes declining the meetings. A bold career plan, if the career is elsewhere.
The candles have witnesses. The budget has left the building.
A shouted argument with a recycling bin is not the calm era. The bin remains unconvinced.
The prime minister is not in this receipt. Bring the missing bridge before the country collapses too.
An apology is not evidence. Put the printed attendance sheet back on the table.
The calendar says optional, and the manager says recorded. The resolution has paperwork.
Seven candles and a bathrobe is not thrift. It is a small indoor economy.
The story closed itself with a confession. Leave one embarrassing fact for the next statement.
The speaker found a feeling where the Judge asked for a fact. Feelings do not come with receipts.
The official position is wobbling, but the evidence is standing upright.

bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host

bad_headlines.text: This is the worst resolution ever.
bad_headlines.why: gives a verdict without naming the evidence

bad_headlines.text: A catastrophic financial implosion has commenced.
bad_headlines.why: uses inflated words instead of a plain picture

bad_headlines.text: You clearly cannot manage your own life.
bad_headlines.why: mocks the player broadly instead of the move

bad_headlines.text: The facts are facts, and the truth is true.
bad_headlines.why: says nothing specific about either step

bad_headlines.text: Oh no, the resolution is dead...

bad_headlines.why: claims a result without naming the charge or the resolution

rules: Give one new observable fact that makes the latest official position harder to believe.
Keep the host speaking in the official style, even when the evidence gets embarrassing.
Skip a link, end the explanation, retract a fact, or change the subject and the chain stops with you.
The Judge rules on the connection and the evidence, never on spelling.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft the next piece of evidence while you wait

validation_messages.empty: No evidence was offered. The official position cannot defend itself.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. This is a statement, not a parliamentary inquiry.
validation_messages.duplicate: That evidence already appeared this match. Find a fresh embarrassment.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Add one fact that follows from {standing_form} and makes the position harder to believe.

judge_out_text: The Judge has stepped out. Nobody adds evidence until they return. {standing_form} still stands, and the official position is not improving.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two players extending a public apology that is getting harder to defend.
Always give one new observable fact in the host's official style. Keep the explanation going while making it look worse.
Good: "The official position is that I am saving money. The bank statement contains a charge for a life-size inflatable hot tub."
Good: "The official position is that I am exercising daily. The gym receptionist has seen me use the cafe twice and the treadmill never."
Bad: "The official position is that I am involved in a national scandal" because the link is skipped.
Bad: "The official position is that I admit everything and will do better" because it ends the explanation.
Bad: "The official position is that I feel ashamed" because a feeling is not evidence.
Never clear the speaker, close the press conference, retract a fact, or undo what stands.
Use plain words and one fact. A receipt, a calendar, a neighbour, a delivery box, a missed alarm. Keep the joke specific.
Adult innuendo and mild profanity are allowed when useful, but do not target identity or protected traits.
Never reuse evidence from this match.
default_move: The official position is that I am still committed. The unopened planner is underneath the takeaway menu.
